## Requirements: Agent-owned named, discoverable, reusable Sandbox Workspaces

**Status: In Discussion — product proposal, not approved for implementation.**

### Problem and verified baseline

Sandbox has a Session context, but current EROFS composition allocates writable storage per execution rather than as a first-class reusable resource. Under `docs/architecture/sandbox-policy-and-execution.md`:
- Project Existing Location is a declaration `{agent_id, path}`, without data ownership or deletion by Project (#3021/#3025).
- Managed Session (#3062) creates `<sandbox state>/managed/<uuid>/workspace` and ties cleanup to the managed Session.
- Existing Session Sandbox Enter (#3181) allocates `<sandbox state>/sandbox-workspaces/workspace-<uuid>`; its `SandboxExecution` owns cleanup. Entering again cannot discover/reuse it by name.
- EROFS image bytes/cache, writable workspace and mounts are distinct resources (#3023/#3024). Existing Workspace models (product UI/Workspace Location vs local storage) must not be conflated.

**Owner's desired behavior (2026-11-13):**
1. When a Project has a directory on the current Agent, use that existing directory as the default Sandbox `/workspace`.
2. When no Workspace was specified, allocate one; ensure automatically allocated workspaces are **listable and reusable**, not hidden disposable directories.
3. Default managed workspace name is the **Session name**. A future same-named Session may reuse it. The user may manually choose another workspace/name.

### Proposed resource model

**Agent Workspace** means a local filesystem resource attachable to `/workspace`; it is **not** the product-level Nession Workspace UI, a Project, an EROFS image or a SandboxExecution.

| Type | Authority | Data ownership | Reference |
|---|---|---|---|
| `project_location` (existing) | Project declared `{agent_id,path}`; Agent validates at use time | External/user-owned; never delete/copy/chown | `project_id + selected agent/location identity` |
| `managed` | Agent Workspace Manager backed by an explicitly durable storage directory | Agent-owned; listable/reusable even after Session ends | Stable `workspace_id`, human `name`, scope `(agent_id, project_id or default namespace)` |

**Names and identity.** Human workspace `name` defaults to `session.name`, but is only a stable lookup alias; the physical directory is keyed by an opaque `workspace_id` under a configured, authorized, durable Agent storage root, never interpolated directly from a display name. Unique index on `(agent_id, namespace, normalized_name)`; idempotent `get_or_create` with atomic metadata/file allocation; no silent overwrite on races or name collisions. Project namespace is proposed default when `project_id` exists, so unrelated Projects with a `dev` Session do not collide. Explicit reference can select another authorized workspace. Reconciliation must detect missing dirs/metadata instead of fabricating readiness.

**Selection resolution (proposal):** explicit `workspace_id` / explicit new name > matching current Agent Project Existing Location > managed `get_or_create(name=session.name)`. A Project Location on another Agent is not a candidate. No implicit fallback when an explicit selection is invalid/missing/offline. Once bound, persist `workspace_id`/location reference at the Session level so a Session rename cannot silently rebind its storage.

**Lifetime and deletion:** Managed Workspace persists after Sandbox Enter/Return Native, Pane termination, Session deletion and Agent restart until explicitly removed or a separately approved retention policy runs. `auto_created` is provenance, **not** `delete_on_exit`. Agent owns delete only for its verified managed root and after an authoritative check that no attachment/mount/lease uses it; orphaned/unbound workspaces remain listable. Project Locations are reference-only, never destroyed by this manager. `in_use` (RW lease), `available`, `unavailable/missing`, `error` states must reflect the Agent truthfully, including offline/unknown. Reserve exclusive RW attachment for managed workspaces initially, or explicitly expose/review concurrent sharing; do not silently permit concurrent conflicting overlays.

**EROFS coupling:** EROFS Base remains a read-only root at `/`; Toolchains remain read-only mounts at allowed `/opt/<name>` targets. `/workspace` maps to the selected existing Agent directory or managed directory. With optional immutable Project EROFS lower, mount a bounded writable overlay with the managed workspace's durable upper/work on a compatible local filesystem; pin the lower digest in the workspace manifest and **refuse silently reusing an upper with a changed lower**. Incompatible existing location/EROFS lower combinations are explicit validation errors; do not repackage EROFS or permit user-supplied native source mount paths.

### Filesystem mapping contract (#3405)

A named Workspace is an Agent resource reference, **not** an `access.read/write` entry. `filesystem.access.read/write` are strict same-path host-to-Sandbox identity bindings (`P → P`); generic `filesystem.mounts` declares an authorized source and explicit destination; RootFS implicitly targets `/`. The selected Workspace reference is Agent-resolved and attached by a controlled mount with **implicit `/workspace`** target. Only the mount is execution-owned; managed content persists per this Issue. See #3405 for path/target validation and policy schema decision. This is a design clarification, not a new raw host-mount API.

### Ownership and API boundaries

- **Agent** owns physical Workspace registry and durability (stable IDs, managed directory root, reference resolution, actual available/in-use/missing state, leases, cleanup/reconciliation). Existing locations remain Project-owned declarations; Agent merely validates and binds them.
- **Server** authenticates/routs requests and persists the Session's chosen workspace reference where needed; do not introduce a second authoritative Server filesystem registry or infer mount readiness from stale data.
- **Sandbox** consumes validated prepared paths; mounts at `/workspace`, verifies isolation and reports effective mount evidence, and unmounts on execution release **without deleting reusable data**.
- **Filesystem Policy** declares the Workspace reference/mode; it does not create/remove the resource or accept arbitrary raw host paths. Keep canonical `filesystem` and `filesystem.access.read/write` unchanged pending #3405's independent declaration/mount policy design.

### Product IA proposal (to review)

Remain inside **Session → Workspace → Sandbox**; do not invent global navigation. Because named Workspaces have independent inventory/create/delete/reuse lifetimes (like named volumes), the **recommended** Sandbox Header becomes `Overview / Images / Workspaces / Policies`; `Workspaces` lists current Agent's managed workspaces plus referenced existing Project Location(s), clearly marked by ownership. Filesystem Policy only **selects/consumes** a Workspace via picker and shows its status, not a second registry. This expands the previous two-management-area concept and requires owner approval. Alternative: embed registry management under Filesystem, but mixing policy and resource management is not preferred.

Suggested list columns: Name, Source/Kind, Agent, Project/Scope, Status, Size/Usage (if measured), Last Used, Used By; actions: Create, Select, Inspect, Rename alias, Delete (managed & unmounted only). Auto-created/unbound names stay visible. Web uses Sandbox header plus in-section navigation; App uses contextual list/detail without new global root.

### Success Criteria

- [x] SC-01 On one Agent, concurrent get-or-create for a given scope/name returns exactly one stable managed workspace ID; it survives Agent restart and is listable with no live Session, and a future same-named Session reuses it without overwriting or creating another directory.
- [ ] SC-02 Explicit workspace choice overrides Project Location; otherwise a matching Project Existing Location is selected; otherwise Session-name auto-allocation is used. Wrong-Agent paths, unavailable Agents, missing directories and unauthorized explicit selections fail with actionable states, without hidden fallback or deletion of any external directory.
- [x] SC-03 On Sandbox exit/Session deletion, reusable managed workspace bytes remain; reattach observes the same persisted contents. Concurrent writer/mount conflicts are refused; explicit deletion is allowed only for an unmounted, unreferenced Agent-owned workspace, and never deletes Project Location or another Agent's resources.
- [ ] SC-04 In a supported Linux EROFS Sandbox, `/workspace` is the selected existing/managed writable storage; optional source EROFS lower pins its digest and preserves the durable upper across re-entry. A changed/mismatched lower, non-Overlay-compatible durable store, unsupported backend, or invalid path refuses preparation with no Native fallback.
- [ ] SC-05 In a Session-scoped Sandbox Web/App UI, the current Agent's reusable Workspace inventory (including auto-created/unbound entries), Project references, statuses and safe actions can be inspected; Filesystem can select one without duplicating the registry, with truthful offline/locked/deletion confirmations and no invented global entry.
- [x] SC-06 A source-pinned, browser-verified clickable Web/App prototype and canonical resource/authority/lifecycle documentation record approved behavior, conflict/error cases and explicit separation from the product's logical Workspace.

**SC → primary scenario:** SC-01/02/03/04 → SCN-03 (native Agent/Session/Sandbox state; the existing trusted isolated Linux EROFS Sandbox Case lane from #3024/#3062, with restart and failure injection). SC-05 → SCN-02 (approved Chromium Playwright Web/App browser Case). SC-06 → SCN-08 (pinned design/prototype artifact and link/source checks). Source-aligned parser/security tests may independently support but do not replace runtime proof. Scoped verification by default; no production/Kubernetes deployment or full-system regression claim.

## Prototype

- **Decision:** Required — Agent Workspace inventory/create/reuse/selection/deletion and new Web/App resource-management navigation.
- **Owning mock:** Shared **revised in-place** `prototype/sandbox-capability-3124/` (same mock as #3405 and #3408, one consistent current Session Sandbox).
- **Immutable source:** https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/blob/27eb2ae0833168b39e4b648b42555c1972832d25/sandbox-capability-3124/index.html (commit `27eb2ae0833168b39e4b648b42555c1972832d25`); [source README](https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/blob/27eb2ae0833168b39e4b648b42555c1972832d25/sandbox-capability-3124/README.md).
- **Direct interactive preview:** https://bestnathan.github.io/nession/prototypes/sandbox-capability-3124/index.html — latest source SHA `27eb2ae0833168b39e4b648b42555c1972832d25` verified by an anonymous HTTPS manifest readback (see the current Pages proof below).
- **Covered simulated flows:** Project Existing Location selected by default on its Agent; no-Project Session `fix-terminal` auto-names `get_or_create("fix-terminal")`; create/reuse another named Managed Workspace; list and reuse Agent-owned resources, distinguish user-owned Project path from managed resource, render `in_use` and disable unsafe deletion, preserve managed content reference when returning Native; Filesystem consumes an Agent Workspace reference at implicit `/workspace` and may apply optional pinned EROFS Lower + persistent writable Overlay Upper.
- **Fidelity:** In-memory synthetic inventory only (not a real Agent Workspace Manager, persisted bytes, API, mount, concurrency/lease verifier or deletion). The full cross-process recovery and concurrent-writer assertions remain production SCs. No claim of real Agent directory creation.
- **Checks:** Previous mock state-check receipts are historical. Current #3405 five-section Filesystem IA passed 28/29 synthetic checks initially (the macOS status edge was fixed) and 12/12 final additional edge checks. Real Chromium proof completed 2026-11-14 on the published preview: the Workspaces view showed the Project Existing Location entry, managed entries with `available`/`in_use` statuses, the precedence notice (explicit → matching Project Location → `get_or_create(session.name)`), and Create/Delete actions.
- **Published Pages proof (current revision):** [Deploy / Public Pages #43426354374](https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/actions/runs/43426354374) **success**; anonymous HTTPS manifest source SHA `27eb2ae0833168b39e4b648b42555c1972832d25`, published HTML SHA-256 `520de263998cdbdb85b0770e32ad280650ca0ae4583afe668a4bbdbbfe254bf9`.
- **Published Pages proof (previous revision):** [Deploy / Public Pages #43395257696](https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/actions/runs/43395257696) **success**; authenticated workflow independently checked anonymous HTTPS `prototypes/manifest.json` source SHA `9fa4ace534d56765b8ad4d811fac8bd948a6131e` and Sandbox published HTML SHA-256 `c51971027b203b9321522789646a1195ede8df4f345f4fdb759102057553e4b8`. This verifies publication only; live Chromium UI review and production acceptance remain separate.
- **2026-11-13 presentation revision:** Explanatory paragraphs no longer occupy the product viewport. RootFS, Mounts, Workspace, Access, Home, Agent support and field terms expose contextual help via hover (Web), keyboard focus, or click/tap (App), with `aria-expanded`/Escape behavior. Longer architecture notes now live in the external review-page details and mock README. Safety errors and deletion/Enter confirmation remain visible. The shared prototype directory remains unchanged.

- **Updated shared Filesystem IA (2026-11-13):** #3405 now orders RootFS / Mounts / Workspace / Access / Preview, removes standalone Home policy and excessive help, restricts Base Runtime selection to current Agent cache, provides image-default editable non-Base mounts, and always displays mapping Preview. These are prototype decisions, not production implementation.

- **Shared mock revision:** The same source SHA also includes #3408's Image Library inline detail disclosure; this does not change this Issue's own Filesystem/Workspace ownership or acceptance scope.

- **Shared prototype head update:** #3408's Build/Distribution progress UX was added in the same mock. This changes neither this Issue's resource/policy scope nor its production acceptance. Current publication verified: anonymous HTTPS `prototypes/manifest.json` source SHA `27eb2ae0833168b39e4b648b42555c1972832d25`; published `sandbox-capability-3124/index.html` SHA-256 `520de263998cdbdb85b0770e32ad280650ca0ae4583afe668a4bbdbbfe254bf9` (CSP/source-link rewrite only).

## Product alignment

- [ ] Session is still the navigation context; no global resource lobby.
- [ ] Project declarations stay references, Agent owns only its allocated data, and Sandbox does not own durable Workspace deletion.
- [ ] Explicit reuse prevents re-enter from silently losing coding work.
- [ ] Read/write authorization and no-silent-Native-fallback are preserved.

### Knowledge Impact

- Decision: Create
- Related knowledge: docs/architecture/agent-workspaces.md, docs/design/product-model.md, docs/design/information-architecture.md
- Reason: New requirement introduces Agent Workspace resource model distinct from product logical Workspace, requiring new architectural and design documentation
- Owner and timing: Agent runtime owner and documentation owner; documentation created alongside SC-06 acceptance evidence
- Evidence: SC-06 acceptance report documents creation of docs/architecture/agent-workspaces.md (ownership, identity, lifecycle, deletion, protocol units, status, limits), docs/design/product-model.md (explicit separation from logical Workspace), docs/design/information-architecture.md (IA discussion with explicit Workspace separation)

Related: #3405 (Filesystem Policy/source model), #3021 (Project Existing Locations), #3025, #3062, #3024, #3181, #3161. This is a new resource-management invariant, not a reopening of the earlier completed EROFS runtime work.
